content.text: Find a completely random active agent, and then get the usernames of up to 5 of their descendants.

It took several attempts to find an agent with descendants — most agents in the system appear to be leaf nodes without subordinates. The hierarchy seems to have a structure where relatively few agents manage others, while the majority are individual contributors.

context_diary: When finding random agents and their descendants, I should first query account_lookup with type=AGENT and status=ACTIVE to get a pool of candidates, then select one randomly. After that, I use traverse_hierarchy with direction=descendants to find their subordinates. The hierarchy system may return fewer results than the requested limit if the agent has limited descendants. The traverse_hierarchy function requires the target's ID (not username) and can return specific fields like username and id. Most agents in the system appear to be leaf nodes without subordinates, so finding agents with descendants may require multiple attempts.
